bib.title: Text Similarity and Clustering (Chapter 6, Text Analytics with Python)

question: How can text similarity be measured between terms and documents, and how can documents be clustered without labels?
contributions: Hand-built term distances (Hamming, Manhattan, Euclidean, Levenshtein, cosine)
Document similarity and ranking by cosine, Hellinger-Bhattacharya and Okapi BM25 on a toy corpus
K-means, affinity propagation and Ward clustering of 100 IMDb movie synopses with MDS visualisation

limits: Toy corpus of 9 documents and 3 queries; no relevance judgements, so metrics are compared only by eye.
Clustering quality is not scored (no silhouette or purity); the author leaves 'which is better' to the reader.
Code is Python 2 era (print statements, scipy itemfreq, html_parser.unescape, DataFrame.ix) and has dated.
Cosine/BM25 are bag-of-words and ignore order and synonyms; semantic similarity (embeddings) is not covered.
Author concedes k-means needs k in advance and can hit local minima; AP is computationally heavy; no production BM25 in nltk/scikit-learn at the time.
practices: Check a distance against the four metric conditions (non-negative, zero iff identical, symmetric, triangle inequality) before using it as a metric (p.267-268).
Use cosine on TF-IDF vectors for documents because it ignores length and order (p.289).
Prefer sklearn cosine_similarity, gensim hellinger() and gensim.matutils.cossim over hand-written versions for large corpora (p.289, p.292).
Use Levenshtein (not Hamming/Manhattan/Euclidean) when terms have unequal length (p.282).
Set min_df and max_df to drop terms in almost all documents before clustering (p.270).
Initialise k-means with kmeans++ and run multiple restarts to avoid local minima (p.302).
Choose k with the elbow method or silhouette coefficient (p.308).
Reduce dimensionality with MDS on a cosine distance matrix to visualise clusters in 2-D (p.304).
Build topic models per cluster to label clusters better than centroid keywords (p.313).

terms.definition: A measure d satisfying non-negativity, d(x,y)=0 iff x=y, symmetry and the triangle inequality
Similarity from the syntax, structure and content of the text
Similarity from the meaning and context of the documents
A bag-of-words document ranking framework based on probabilistic relevancy, with parameters k1 and b
Euclidean norm of the difference of the square roots of two vectors divided by sqrt(2); an f-divergence
Clustering by message passing (responsibility and availability) between data points, yielding exemplars, with no preset k
Linkage criterion that merges the pair of clusters giving the least increase in within-cluster variance
